named_classical_import.name: Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt theorem

pin.kind: public secondary encyclopedia page fetched 2026-10-27 17:24:41 PDT; statement only, not a primary proof

named_classical_import.statement_verbatim: Let L be a Lie algebra over K and X a totally ordered basis of L. A canonical monomial over X is a finite sequence (x_1, x_2, ..., x_n) of elements of X which is non-decreasing in the order <=, that is, x_1 <= x_2 <= ... <= x_n. Extend h to all canonical monomials as follows: if (x_1, x_2, ..., x_n) is a canonical monomial, let h(x_1, x_2, ..., x_n) = h(x_1) h(x_2) ... h(x_n). Then h is injective on the set of canonical monomials and the image of this set forms a basis for U(L) as a K-vector space. [h is the canonical K-linear map from L into the universal enveloping algebra U(L); the empty canonical monomial corresponds to 1.]
named_classical_import.use_rule: Quote this statement at each use, state the hypotheses it is applied under and the consequence if it were false. No PBW proof text, textbook normal-form body or count is imported; every other step, including the identification of U of a free Lie algebra with the tensor algebra, must be proved in writing.
